why.headline: Quick, low side steps keep you square to the ball.

claims.text: In studies of adult keepers, most of a match was slow. The saves came in short, fast bursts.
You must dive well to both sides. In academy keepers, weaker-side dives used the trunk less well.
Early-teen players did jump or footwork drills twice a week. After 6 weeks, zigzag runs were 2 to 4% faster.
Boys in their early teens trained twice weekly. After 6 weeks, a side-to-side shuttle was 0.3 to 3.8% faster.

keep_up.text: Keep training it every week to keep gains coming. In one youth study, jump gains lasted 8 weeks after training stopped. Everyone improves at their own pace.

map.plain: The muscle on the side of your hip

note.text: Side-step studies measured these muscles in adults; none measured them in teens.

claims.text: In adults, side steps in a low squat worked hip muscles more.
Across youth studies, jump training made turns quicker. Older teens tended to gain a bit more.

limits.text: No study has tested the lateral shuffle alone in goalkeepers. The youth trials mixed several drills.
